name: small-fix-r1-architect-1792387259174
idea: In src/text.js, truncate(text, max) is meant to return a string of at most max characters, ending in "..." when it had to cut the text. It sometimes returns something longer than max. Fix it and leave the other behaviour alone. This fix ships after a CI run on GitHub. Do m1 yourself. milestones.title: truncate() never exceeds max
milestones.plan:
## Objective
Make `truncate(text, max)` in `src/text.js` obey its contract: the returned string is at most `max` characters, and it ends in `...` when the text had to be cut.

## Change
- Only `truncate` is modified. When `text.length <= max`, return the text unchanged.
- Otherwise return the head shortened so that head + `...` fits in `max` characters. For `max` smaller than the ellipsis length, return the longest string that fits `max` (i.e. `'.'.repeat(max)` for `max > 0`), so the length limit always holds.
- `capitalize` and everything else is untouched.

## Tests
- Add cases: cut text ends in `...` and respects `max`; exactly-`max` text is returned unchanged; very small `max` (0-3) obeys the length limit; existing tests still pass.
- Verify with `pnpm test`.
